comparison: Both evaluations support the electrophysiological evidence for Y404W gain-of-function and Y404A loss-of-function mutations (C5-C7, C33-C34, C36-C37). OpenEval additionally references dose-response data (C82) and quantitative EC50 values, while peer review emphasizes the compelling nature of the functional demonstration. Both rate these claims as SUPPORTED.

Both evaluations agree that the Y404W and Y404A mutants can still be modulated by agonists and antagonists (C8-C9, C35, C76). OpenEval notes the distinction from pore-locking proline mutants, while peer review emphasizes that Tyr404 is distant from ligand binding sites. However, OpenEval R4 does not address C10 (screening utility claim), which peer review includes and supports. Both rate the functional modulation claims as SUPPORTED.

Both evaluations support the high-resolution cryo-EM structure of Y404W TRPML1 in the open state (C38-C44). OpenEval emphasizes the 2.86 Å resolution and local resolution details (C75, C80-C81), while peer review focuses on the allosteric mechanism whereby W404 provides van der Waals contacts causing S4 bending and pore opening. Both rate these structural claims as SUPPORTED.

Both evaluations support the PI(4,5)P2-bound structure and its allosteric inhibition mechanism (C48-C54, C72, C74, C77). OpenEval provides more comprehensive coverage including additional structural details (C11-C12, C70-C71, C73, C83-C84) and emphasizes the distinct binding mode compared to PI(3,5)P2. Peer review also includes the S1 movement mechanism (C55-C56) which OpenEval addresses separately in R11. Both rate these claims as SUPPORTED.

Both evaluations support the structural observation of sphingomyelin (or phosphocholine) density at the agonist/antagonist binding site (C57-C61, C78-C79). OpenEval additionally references functional data showing SM reduces SF-51 activation (C13-C14, C62-C63), while peer review focuses on accepting the structural density observation. Both appropriately note the tentative identification of the lipid. Both rate these claims as SUPPORTED.

Both evaluations address the sphingomyelin antagonist effect and competitive mechanism (C62-C69). OpenEval rates these claims as SUPPORTED based on functional data showing SM both reduces agonist activation and mitigates antagonist inhibition, while peer review rates them as UNCERTAIN, noting that the competitive binding mechanism is a proposed hypothesis rather than definitively proven. This represents a key disagreement in confidence level. OpenEval additionally addresses pH requirements (C85-C86) not mentioned in peer review.

Both evaluations support the background and foundational claims about TRPML1 function, disease relevance, and regulatory mechanisms (C1-C2, C15-C20). These are established facts from the literature that neither evaluation questions. Both rate these claims as SUPPORTED.

Both evaluations address prior structural knowledge about TRPML1 gating mechanisms (C4, C28-C32). OpenEval includes broader background claims (C3, C21-C27) establishing the foundation for the study, while peer review (R7) focuses on the global conformational change mechanism and accepts the allosteric gating mechanism as partially supported by functional data. Peer review also includes C75 (structural comparison). Both rate these claims as SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap on background claims (C21-C25) about TRPML1 structure and function. OpenEval R2 covers extensive prior structural knowledge (C3-C4, C21-C31), while peer R9 focuses on established background facts from literature (C1-C2, C15-C25). Both rate these foundational claims as SUPPORTED.

Both evaluations support claims about Arg403's dual role and the R403C patient variant (C45-C47). OpenEval emphasizes the structural analysis and appropriate citations, while peer review accepts these as established context from previously published structures. Peer review R10 also includes additional background claims (C26-C27, C70-C71) not in OpenEval R7. Both rate these claims as SUPPORTED.

Both evaluations address the S1 movement mechanism (C55-C56) showing how PI(4,5)P2 binding restricts S1 movement and inhibits channel gating. OpenEval R11 focuses specifically on these mechanistic claims based on structural comparisons, while peer R4 includes these as part of a broader evaluation of the PI(4,5)P2 inhibition mechanism. Both rate these claims as SUPPORTED.

Both evaluations reference the high-resolution PI(4,5)P2-bound structure (C11-C12, C73). OpenEval R8 provides comprehensive structural details about the PI(4,5)P2 binding mechanism, while peer R8 (editor's summary) accepts the cryo-EM structures as convincingly supporting allosteric regulation claims. Limited overlap in specific claim IDs but both address the same structural contribution. Both rate these claims as SUPPORTED.

Both evaluations address the sphingomyelin structural observation and mechanistic explanation (C13-C14). OpenEval R9 includes comprehensive coverage of SM binding and functional effects (C13-C14, C57-C63, C78-C79), while peer R11 focuses on accepting the structural observation of endogenous lipid and the plausibility of the mechanistic explanation. Both rate these claims as SUPPORTED.

OpenEval R5 addresses C10 (screening utility claim) and rates it as UNCERTAIN because no actual screening experiments are presented to validate the assertion. Peer R2 includes C10 among claims about continued ligand responsiveness and rates it as SUPPORTED, viewing the mutants as useful tools based on their functional properties. This represents a disagreement in evaluation confidence.

OpenEval R5 evaluates C10 as UNCERTAIN, noting it is a forward-looking conclusion requiring future experimental validation. No corresponding isolated peer review evaluation focuses specifically on this claim, though peer R2 includes it among supported claims about the mutants' utility.
